why: Doc sentence confirmed verbatim (observability.md:41, whole line; the trailing second sentence 'The most common configuration sends all three signals over OTLP HTTP to a collector.' does not reverse it). The cited evidence is real but the finding's central factual claims are false. (1) 'There is no telemetry emitter' is wrong: packages/shared/src/telemetry/usage-metrics.ts is a full OTLP/HTTP metrics exporter (interval flush, shutdown drain, delta/cumulative temporality, nessy.token.usage + nessy.cost.usage sums) and packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/otlp-telemetry.ts is a full OTLP/HTTP logs exporter (batched resourceLogs, six-event closed set, HMAC-salted workspace/session hashes, one retry). (2) 'no CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY ... reader exists' is wrong: usage-metrics.ts:301-306 telemetryOptedIn() reads env.NESSY_ENABLE_TELEMETRY as primary and env.CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY as the compat alias, and it is the gate for BOTH signals (otlp-telemetry.ts:43,200). 'no OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER / OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER reader' is wrong: otelExporterDisabled() (usage-metrics.ts:318-325) reads both selectors and honours 'none' as a hard disable, called at usage-metrics.ts:336 and otlp-telemetry.ts:202. (3) The claim that the managed-settings allowlist passes OTEL vars through 'without anything consuming them' is the inference that fails: parseConfig in both exporters consumes OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, _HEADERS, _TIMEOUT and OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL — four of the five allowlisted entries — plus the per-signal _METRICS_ENDPOINT/_LOGS_ENDPOINT overrides and _METRICS_TEMPORALITY_PREFERENCE. (4) Consequence check one layer up and one layer down: both are wired end to end, not inert. storage-runtime.ts:272-273 constructs them; SessionManager.recordUsageMetrics (:3004) is called from the single usage-event site at :18382 whose own comment says 'The one emission site every backend passes through ... Pi, the Claude SDK, Codex and Nestor Cloud all land here'; emitPiTelemetry (:2984) feeds the log exporter; shutdown drains at :19246; and both hosts pass them through (apps/electron/src/main/index.ts:723, packages/server/src/index.ts:241). (5) The parenthetical 'the Pi and Codex runtimes, which are the shipped defaults, emit nothing' is exactly backwards — Pi is the only runtime carrying BOTH signals, since the harness log exporter is deliberately Pi-gated (:2988) while metrics are deliberately not provider-gated. The coverage map already records this page as built (2026-07-31-claude-coverage-map.md:184, row B2, green). Not an inert-worklist section 3 decision; the residual gaps are recorded deliberate fork decisions (bank-fork privacy posture in the usage-metrics header, NESSY_ prefix rename with Claude compat alias).
correctedState: Two of the three documented signals are implemented as real OTLP/HTTP exporters, gated on exactly the documented switch plus exporter selectors. Metrics: packages/shared/src/telemetry/usage-metrics.ts — createUsageMetrics() built at packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/storage-runtime.ts:273, fed for EVERY backend (Pi, Claude SDK, Codex, Nestor Cloud) at SessionManager.ts:18382 via recordUsageMetrics (:3004), interval flush plus shutdown drain. Log events: packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/otlp-telemetry.ts — createPiOtlpTelemetry() built at storage-runtime.ts:272, Pi-gated by design at SessionManager.ts:2988, drained at :19246. Both hosts wire them (apps/electron/src/main/index.ts:723, packages/server/src/index.ts:241). The opt-in is telemetryOptedIn() (usage-metrics.ts:301) — NESSY_ENABLE_TELEMETRY primary, CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY compat alias — and otelExporterDisabled() (:318) honours OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER=none and OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER=none as hard disables. What is genuinely absent, and is the only defensible residue of this finding: the TRACES signal. There are no spans — no OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER or CLAUDE_CODE_ENHANCED_TELEMETRY_BETA reader, no resourceSpans payload, no tracer. Per the page's own table traces are beta and require the extra beta flag. Also deliberately not implemented, with the reason recorded in the usage-metrics.ts header: the OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS / _ASSISTANT_RESPONSES / _RAW_API_BODIES content channels (bank fork — conversation content must not leave the operator's machine) and the monitoring-usage.md:442 standard-attribute table including session.id and user.id (no per-user or per-session identifier is exported). OTEL_SERVICE_NAME and OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES are not read; service.name is hardcoded 'nessy-desktop'. Metric names are renamed nessy.token.usage / nessy.cost.usage under the fork-wide rename.
